title: Reference-independent analysis of RADseq data from a single sample
author: Bradley J Till
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bdtji6kn

steps.title: Prepare Genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Extract and concentrate genomic DNA of suitable quality and quantity for next-generation sequencing (NGS).

steps.title: Model Genome Representation with RestrictionDigest
steps.instruction: Use the RestrictionDigest Perl module to model the percentage of the genome represented in a specific molecular weight range for a chosen restriction enzyme using a closely related species' reference genome.

substeps.instruction: Download and install RestrictionDigest software.
Download the reference genome assembly of a closely related species (fasta as .fa or .fna) and place it in the RestrictionDigest directory.
Create a Perl script (e.g., bthunbergii_haeIII.pl) in the RestrictionDigest directory using the Ubuntu Text Editor.
Configure the script: set the path to the genome fasta file, specify the restriction nucleases (e.g., HaeIII), define the size range (e.g., 350-700 bp), and set the output directory.
Execute the script via terminal: 'perl [yourscript].pl'.
Open the 'digestion_summary...' file to review length and fragment ranges.

steps.title: Determine DNA Input and Sequencing Throughput
steps.instruction: Calculate the required starting genomic DNA amount and the necessary sequencing throughput based on the modeled genome fraction and expected genome size.

substeps.instruction: Calculate starting DNA: Divide the required library preparation material (e.g., 200 ng) by the modeled genome fraction (e.g., 0.179) to determine the minimum starting genomic DNA (e.g., 1.1 micrograms). Use a larger amount to account for recovery losses.
Estimate unique base pairs: Multiply the expected genome size (e.g., 1.5 Gb) by the genome fraction and the fragment range (e.g., 268 Mbps).

Adjust throughput based on library results: If a percentage of fragments fall below a certain size (e.g., 75% ≤ 395 bp), adjust the unique base pair estimation and purchase raw sequencing data (e.g., 1 Gb) to achieve desired coverage (e.g., 11.9x).

steps.title: Isolate DNA and Sequence
steps.instruction: Isolate the selected size range of genomic DNA from an agarose gel and have the library preparation, sequencing, de-multiplexing, and trimming performed by a service provider.

steps.title: Evaluate Raw Fastq Data
steps.instruction: Assess the quality of the raw compressed fastq files (fastq.gz or fq.gz) provided by the sequencing service.

substeps.instruction: Install and run FastQC (v0.11.9) using the GUI.
Verify that sequence quality scores match expectations for the chemistry and read length.

steps.title: Process Fastq Files with Stacks
steps.instruction: Filter and process the raw reads using the Stacks pipeline to prepare them for loci creation.

substeps.instruction: Install Stacks (v2.52); on Ubuntu, install gobjc++ and zlib1g-dev first.
Move fq.gz files into the Stacks directory and create an output directory (e.g., radtagsoutputdirectory).
Run process_radtags: 'process_radtags -1 read1.fq.gz -2 read2.fq.gz -o ./radtagsoutputdirectory -c -q -r -e [enzyme]' (e.g., -e haeIII).

steps.title: Interleave Paired-End Reads
steps.instruction: Combine paired-end read files into a single interleaved fastq file using BBmap.

substeps.instruction: Install BBmap from the JGI user guide.
Move the processed fastq.gz files (excluding those with 'rem' in the title) into the bbmap directory.
Execute reformat.sh: './reformat.sh in1=read1.fastq.gz in2=read2.fastq.gz out=interleaved.fq.gz' (e.g., W2pi.fq.gz).

steps.title: Create Loci with ustacks
steps.instruction: Generate loci from the interleaved fastq file using the ustacks program.

substeps.instruction: Move the interleaved file (e.g., W2pi.fq.gz) to the Stacks directory and create a 'stacksout' output directory.
Run ustacks: 'ustacks -f W2pi.fq.gz -o ./stacksout -i 1 -p [threads]' (e.g., -p 64).

steps.title: Create Loci Catalog with cstacks
steps.instruction: Build a catalog of loci using cstacks, which requires a population map file.

substeps.instruction: Create a 'popmap' file: a plain text, tab-delimited file with two columns (e.g., 'W2pi1') and save it in the Stacks directory.
Run cstacks: 'cstacks -P ./stacksout -M ./popmap -n 4 -p [threads]' (e.g., -p 64).

steps.title: Search Consensus Loci with sstacks
steps.instruction: Search the ustacks loci against the cstacks catalog using sstacks.

substeps.instruction: Run sstacks: 'sstacks -P ./stacksout -M ./popmap -p [threads]' (e.g., -p 64).

steps.title: Generate BAM Alignment File
steps.instruction: Convert the results to a BAM formatted alignment file using tsv2bam.

substeps.instruction: Run tsv2bam: 'tsv2bam -P ./ustacksout -M ./popmap/popmap -t [threads]' (e.g., -t 64).

steps.title: Identify SNPs with gstacks
steps.instruction: Identify single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) using gstacks.

substeps.instruction: Run gstacks: 'gstacks -P ./ustacksout -M ./popmap/popmap -t [threads]' (e.g., -t 64).

steps.title: Export VCF and Fasta Files
steps.instruction: Use the populations tool to create standard output files for downstream analysis.

substeps.instruction: Create VCF file: 'populations -P ./ustacksout --vcf -t [threads]' (e.g., -t 64).
Create Fasta loci file: 'populations -P ./ustacksout --fasta-loci -t [threads]' (e.g., -t 64).

steps.title: Perform Preliminary Data Analysis
steps.instruction: Evaluate the success of the experimental design by reviewing the Stacks log files.

substeps.instruction: Check gstacks.log for the number of loci, mean loci size, and mean coverage.
Check populations.log for unique base pairs and heterozygous variation.
